strapiBlog.title: Top Upcoming Mega Projects in Dubai 2026
strapiBlog.short_description: Dubai’s relentless pursuit of innovation continues to shape its future, with visionary mega projects redefining luxury living, commercial landscapes, and urban infrastructure.

data.text:
Dubai’s relentless pursuit of innovation continues to shape its future, with visionary mega projects redefining luxury lifestyle at its best. As the city strengthens its position as a global epicenter for business and tourism, the upcoming Dubai projects in 2026 promise to push architectural and technological boundaries like never before. 

From opulent residential communities and state-of-the-art commercial hubs to transformative infrastructure and futuristic attractions, these groundbreaking developments will elevate the city’s global stature. 
So buckle up and join us as we explore some of the most anticipated Dubai mega projects - both under construction and set for launch!

Dubai Upcoming Projects to Look Out For

Dubai’s real estate landscape is evolving with new projects that blend luxury, innovation, and sustainability.

Dubai Creek Tower

Dubai Creek Tower is one of the most talked-about new developments in Dubai. It stands out as an observation landmark envisioned by Emaar and designed by Santiago Calatrava. 

The project was unveiled ahead of the COVID-19 pandemic, and major foundation milestones were publicly shared in the years that followed. However, Emaar has just announced a new design for the tower and aims to issue a tender within the next three months. 

Ghaf Woods

Building on the standout success of Tilal Al Ghaf, Majid Al Futtaim introduced another flagship destination, Ghaf Woods. It is one of the most anticipated upcoming residential projects in Dubai. 

Set beside Global Village, this eco-led community is being positioned as Dubai’s first “forest living” address, designed to immerse residents in a genuine woodland setting where nature shapes daily life and every detail supports a greener way of living.

Planned as a thriving habitat for more than 20 bird species, Ghaf Woods will feature more trees than people and aims to keep outdoor temperatures up to 5°C cooler than surrounding areas. With its destination-style appeal, it is expected to become a must-visit once complete, reinforcing its status among Dubai mega projects. 

The community will also offer a varied residential mix, from well-planned apartments to premium penthouses, available in multiple layouts and sizes to suit different lifestyle priorities.

Six Senses Dubai Marina

Six Senses Residences Dubai Marina is one of Dubai’s new building projects set to make a global statement. Rising 122 floors, once completed, it will be the world’s tallest residential tower. 

The development will include 251 ultra-luxury homes, from elegant 2-bedroom residences to expansive 5-bedroom triplexes, alongside exclusive duplexes and penthouses designed for added space and privacy.

Wellness is the main differentiator, with 61,250 sq. ft of amenities spread across four dedicated levels, including a standout pool on the 109th floor. 

Each home is designed to support sustainability, well-being, and comfort, integrating Sleep With Six Senses bedroom features, biophilic elements, and classical feng shui principles, all framed by panoramic views of the Arabian Sea and Dubai’s landmark skyline.

Regent Residences at Marasi Marina

Another new building project in Dubai is the Regent Residences at Marasi Marina. It is a $1 billion development that promises to set new standards in luxury waterfront living. 

Comprising two 591-foot skyscrapers connected by an exclusive sky pool, the project offers 60 lavish apartments, each exceeding 6,500 square feet and featuring private balcony pools with panoramic views of the Burj Khalifa. 

The crown jewel of the development is a sprawling 35,000-square-foot penthouse, complete with six bedrooms, a private gym, and a 43-foot sky pool. Residents will also have access to an 82-foot indoor lap pool, private dining spaces, a state-of-the-art gym, integrated retail outlets, and lush green spaces.

  • Completion Date: 2027
  • Location: Marasi Marina, Business Bay, Dubai
  • Developer: Sankari Properties

Urban Oasis by Missoni

Bringing the renowned Italian fashion house's signature style to Dubai, Urban Oasis by Missoni is a 38-story residential tower located adjacent to the Dubai Water Canal. The development offers a range of one to four-bedroom apartments as well as penthouses, each meticulously designed with Missoni's distinctive aesthetic. 

Residents will have access to exclusive amenities, including a swimming pool, fully equipped fitness center, and elegantly designed communal areas, all reflecting the brand's commitment to luxury and sophistication.

  • Completion Date: To be announced
  • Location: Business Bay, Dubai
  • Developer: Dar Al Arkan Real Estate Development Company

Ciel Dubai Marina

Set to claim the title of the world's tallest hotel, Ciel Dubai Marina is an architectural masterpiece soaring over 365 meters with 82 floors. Designed by the renowned NORR Group, the hotel will feature 1,042 luxurious rooms, including 150 premium suites. 

Guests and residents will be treated to exceptional amenities, such as a rooftop infinity pool offering unparalleled views of the city and coastline, multiple world-class dining venues, and a state-of-the-art fitness center.

The hotel is nearing completion. The main contractor, China Railway 18th Bureau Group (CR18BG), is expected to hand over the tower in February 2025, with the hotel's official opening slated for the end of 2025. 

  • Completion Date: 2025
  • Location: Dubai Marina, Dubai
  • Developer: The First Group

Burj Azizi

Adding to the impressive roster of Dubai mega projects, Burj Azizi is an ambitious development set to become the world's second-tallest building. 

It is a monumental 725-meter skyscraper under construction on Sheikh Zayed Road. Scheduled for completion in 2028, this 131-story architectural marvel will feature luxury residences, an all-suite seven-star hotel inspired by seven cultural themes, and a vertical retail center spanning seven floors. 

Residents and visitors will have access to world-record-breaking amenities, including the highest hotel lobby on level 11, the highest nightclub on level 126, and the highest observation deck on level 130, offering unparalleled panoramic views of Dubai. 

As the only freehold property on Sheikh Zayed Road, Burj Azizi is set to redefine luxury living and solidify Dubai's status as a global leader in architectural innovation.

  • Completion Date: 2028
  • Location: Sheikh Zayed Road
  • Developer: Azizi Developments

Ongoing Transportation Projects in Dubai

These ongoing transportation initiatives are a testament to Dubai’s dedication to sustainable urban growth and its ambition to lead the world in smart mobility solutions.

 As part of Dubai mega projects, these developments aim to enhance connectivity, reduce congestion, and set new benchmarks for innovative transit infrastructure.

Al Maktoum International Airport

Al Maktoum International Airport (DWC) is the centrepiece of one of Dubai’s biggest active transport infrastructure expansions. In 2024, Dubai approved designs and began work on a new passenger terminal as part of an AED 128 billion programme that is intended to make DWC the world’s largest airport when fully operational.

Counted among one of the most anticipated UAE mega projects, it targets an ultimate capacity of 260 million passengers a year and includes major upgrades such as five runways. 

Dubai Metro Blue Line

The Dubai Metro Blue Line is an upcoming addition to Dubai's rapid transit network, designed to enhance connectivity across key urban areas. Spanning 30 kilometers, the line will feature 14 stations, with 15.5 kilometers of underground tracks and 14.5 kilometers elevated. It will link significant neighborhoods, including 

  • Mirdif
  • Al Warqa
  • International City
  • Dubai Silicon Oasis
  • Academic City
  • Ras Al Khor Industrial Area
  • Dubai Creek Harbour

Interchange stations are planned at Creek (Green Line), Centrepoint (Red Line), and International City 1, facilitating seamless transfers within the metro system.

It is one of the top Dubai upcoming projects with the aim to alleviate road congestion by 20% in critical areas and is projected to serve approximately 200,000 passengers daily upon its expected operational date of September 9, 2029. The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) awarded the AED 20.5 billion ($5.6 billion) construction contract to a consortium comprising Turkey's MAPA and Limak, along with China's CRRC, in December 2024.

This strategic development is anticipated to boost property values near stations by up to 25% and provide efficient travel times ranging from 10 to 25 minutes across various neighborhoods. 

Etihad Rail

Etihad Rail’s passenger service is scheduled to launch in 2026, with stations becoming operational in phases throughout the year. 

The 900 km passenger rail corridor is planned to connect 11 cities across all seven emirates, with trains running at up to 200 km/h and a target of 36 million passengers per year by 2030.

Journey-time projections shared for the national passenger service include Abu Dhabi to Dubai in about 50 minutes, Dubai to Fujairah in about 50 minutes, Abu Dhabi to Al Ruwais in about 1 hour 10 minutes, and Abu Dhabi to Fujairah in about 1 hour 40 minutes. 

A separate high-speed rail link between Abu Dhabi and Dubai has also been referenced, aiming to cut travel time to around 30 minutes at speeds of up to 350 km/h. The station locations are as follows:

  • Dubai: Jumeirah Golf Estates
  • Sharjah: University City
  • Sharjah: Al Dhaid
  • Fujairah: Al Hilal
  • Abu Dhabi: Mohammed bin Zayed City
  • Abu Dhabi: Al Dhannah
  • Abu Dhabi: Al Faya
  • Abu Dhabi: Al Sila
  • Abu Dhabi: Al Mirfa
  • Abu Dhabi: Madinat Zayed
  • Abu Dhabi: Mezairaa

Flying Taxis

As part of Dubai upcoming projects, the city is gearing up to launch flying taxis, marking a revolutionary shift in urban transportation. This futuristic mode of travel is designed to ease congestion, reduce travel time, and offer a sustainable alternative to traditional road transport. 

With Dubai’s commitment to pioneering smart mobility solutions, flying taxis are set to become a key milestone in Dubai projects aimed at redefining city transportation.

  • In February 2024, Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) signed an agreement with Joby Aviation, a California-based eVTOL (electric vertical take-off and landing) manufacturer, to introduce air taxis in Dubai.
  • The initial launch phase is set for 2025, with full commercial operations expected by 2026.
  • The project is also backed by Archer Aviation and Skyports Infrastructure, ensuring that Dubai becomes one of the first cities in the world to deploy an Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) network.

Dubai’s flying taxis will initially operate from four key vertiports, strategically located to provide efficient and quick connectivity across major destinations:

  • Dubai International Airport (DXB)
  • Downtown Dubai (near Burj Khalifa)
  • Dubai Marina
  • Palm Jumeirah

Hyperloop Dubai

Dubai is taking a bold step toward the future of high-speed transportation with its latest underground transit initiatives. Among them is the Dubai Loop, a cutting-edge project developed in collaboration with Elon Musk’s The Boring Company. This 17-kilometer network will feature 11 stations, aiming to transport over 20,000 passengers per hour using electric vehicles capable of reaching speeds of 160 km/h. 

As part of Dubai's future projects, this system is designed to provide a faster, more efficient alternative to traditional road transport, reducing congestion and enhancing urban mobility. While inspired by the Hyperloop concept, which envisions passenger pods traveling at speeds over 1,000 km/h through low-pressure tubes, the Dubai Loop prioritizes an immediate and practical implementation of underground electric transit. No official timeline for completion has been disclosed yet.

Meanwhile, Dubai’s earlier Hyperloop ambitions have seen mixed progress. In 2016, Hyperloop Transportation Technologies (HyperloopTT) conducted a feasibility study for a high-speed corridor between Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, with a proposed travel time of under 15 minutes.

Soon-to-be Launched Dubai Mega Projects

The golden city is set to redefine urban living and environmental sustainability with a series of ambitious mega projects slated for 2025.

These Dubai future projects encompass innovative residential, commercial, and ecological developments, each designed to enhance the city's global standing and commitment to sustainable growth.

Dubai Reefs

Spearheaded by URB, Dubai Reefs is envisioned as a floating sustainable city dedicated to marine research, regeneration, and ecotourism.

It is one of the most anticipated UAE mega projects that aims to establish the world's largest artificial reef. It will cover 200 square kilometers, to support over 1 billion corals and 100 million mangrove trees.

This self-sufficient community will feature residential, hospitality, retail, educational, and research facilities, all powered by renewable energy sources such as solar and hydropower. Additionally, regenerative ocean farming will contribute to food security and promote a green economy by creating more than 30,000 jobs. 

Dubai Magroves

Another visionary project by URB, Dubai Mangroves, aims to plant over 100 million mangrove trees along a 72-kilometer stretch of coastline, marking the world's largest coastal regeneration initiative.

This endeavor seeks to enhance biodiversity, combat climate change by sequestering approximately 1.23 million tonnes of CO2 annually, and protect coastal areas from erosion. The development will include educational and recreational facilities such as the Mangrove Visitor Hub, a botanical museum, and a Nature Reserve Conservation Center, fostering environmental stewardship among residents and visitors. 

The Island by Wasl

Initially announced in 2017, The Island is a luxury development situated near the iconic Burj Al Arab. In November 2023, Wasl awarded a construction contract to China State Construction Engineering Corporation, reaffirming the project's progression. 

It is counted among the new construction projects in Dubai. The development will feature 1,400 hotel rooms under renowned brands such as MGM Grand, Bellagio, and Aria. While earlier plans considered incorporating a casino, recent updates indicate the project will proceed without this feature.

Hatta Beach

As part of the Hatta Master Development Plan, Hatta Beach is a transformative project approved in January 2024. Central to this development is a 10,000-square-meter engineered 'Crystal Lagoon,' surrounded by diverse leisure amenities. 

The plan also encompasses eco-friendly hotels, luxury resorts, cable cars traversing Hatta Dam, waterfalls, hiking and biking trails, and the restoration of Wadi Lim Lake. Efforts to enhance UNESCO World Heritage sites, develop Hatta Souq with 70 commercial units, and introduce new attractions at Hatta Heritage Village underscore the commitment to preserving cultural heritage while promoting tourism.

Under Construction Projects in Dubai

These under construction projects in Dubai promise unmatched luxury, innovative design, and world-class amenities for future homeowners.

Palm Jebel Ali

Palm Jebel Ali is considered one of the top upcoming Dubai mega projects and is under development currently. Originally launched in 2002, the project experienced delays due to the 2008 financial crisis but was revitalized in 2023. The development is set to feature 80 hotels and resorts, with the first residential properties expected to be handed over in 2027. 

While specific completion dates for the entire project have not been officially announced, significant progress is underway, with major contracts awarded for infrastructure and luxury villa construction. 

The World Islands

The World Islands, an ambitious archipelago of 300 man-made islands off the coast of Dubai, is experiencing a resurgence in development after years of dormancy.

Recent initiatives, such as the opening of the Anantara World Islands Dubai Resort, have injected new life into the area, attracting both tourists and investors. Despite these advancements, the complete realization of The World Islands is projected to take at least another decade, as developers navigate logistical challenges and substantial costs associated with construction.

This ongoing development underscores Dubai's commitment to innovative and expansive urban planning, positioning The World Islands as a significant component of Dubai new construction endeavors.

Dubai Islands

As one of the prominent under construction projects in Dubai, Dubai Islands is poised to redefine urban coastal living and enhance the emirate's appeal as a premier global destination.

It was formerly known as Deira Islands. Encompassing 15.3 square kilometers, the project aims to introduce over 80 hotels and resorts, adding 40 kilometers of coastline and 21 kilometers of pristine beaches to Dubai's landscape. Recent advancements include the launch of Edgewater Residences by MGS Development, featuring three elegant 12-story towers with semi-fitted apartments and a host of amenities. 

Other New Developments in Dubai

The golden city is set to redefine urban living and environmental sustainability with a series of ambitious mega projects slated for 2026.

These Dubai future projects encompass innovative residential, commercial, and ecological developments, each designed to enhance the city's global standing and commitment to sustainable growth.

Dubai Museum of Art

Another one of Dubai's upcoming projects is the Dubai Museum of Art (DUMA). It is set to float above the waters of Dubai Creek. Unveiled by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the museum will be a five-storey structure designed by acclaimed Japanese architect Tadao Ando. 

Its architectural concept is inspired by the sea and pearls, reflecting Dubai’s heritage while reshaping the city’s cultural skyline. Planned as more than an exhibition venue, DUMA will include galleries across the first and second floors, a restaurant and VIP lounge on the third, plus ground and basement levels. 

The museum will also host talks, panel discussions, educational programmes, and art fairs, supported by a library, study rooms, and training initiatives aimed at developing future creative leaders. 

Dubai Square

As Dubai continues to scale up its next generation of lifestyle destinations, Emaar has unveiled Dubai Square at Dubai Creek Harbour, a mixed-use project planned to bring residential living and a major retail hub together in one integrated district. 

At the centre will be Dubai Square Mall, which Emaar has indicated is targeted to open in around three years, positioning it as a major addition to the city’s evolving shopping and entertainment landscape.

Designed around future-ready convenience, the mall is being promoted for its sheer scale, with reports citing an estimated AED 180 billion investment and a footprint described as multiple times larger than Downtown Dubai. 

It will cater to the growing electric vehicle market with dedicated facilities, follow a drive-through concept aligned with smart mobility, and utilise AI-powered solutions for a more seamless shopping experience. The architecture is also planned to lean into immersive design, featuring skylights, LED technology, glazed roofs, expansive glass windows, and green landscaping to create a sophisticated destination-style environment.

Therme Dubai

New developments in Dubai of mega-scale are moving beyond shopping and skyline icons into experience-driven wellness, and Therme Dubai is a standout example. Planned for Zabeel Park and targeted to open in 2028, the AED 2 billion resort is being positioned as the world’s tallest wellbeing resort, designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with a concept they describe as “islands in the sky.”

Set across roughly 500,000 sq ft with a 100-metre structure, Therme Dubai is designed to welcome around 1.7 million visitors annually and blend relaxation with entertainment. Key features include a massive interactive park, the world’s largest indoor botanical garden, three 18-metre waterfalls, and a headline 4,500 sq m indoor and terrace pool for year-round use. 

The experience will be organised into three zones: 

  • Restore (thermal rejuvenation with saunas, steam rooms, and mineral baths)
  • Relax (adult-focused pools and treatments)
  • Play (family-friendly fun with 15 water slides and experiential art)

Sustainability plans include recycling 90% of thermal pool water and meeting 80% of fresh-air and cooling requirements through clean energy sources.

faqs.question: What are the Mega Projects in Dubai in 2026?

data.answer: Dubai’s mega projects in 2026 are largely centred on transport, infrastructure, and destination-scale developments such as Etihad Rail, Dubai Square, and Therme Dubai.

faqs.question: What is the next big project in Dubai?

data.answer: The next major project to come is widely expected to be the Etihad Rail passenger network, scheduled to begin operations in 2026 with phased station openings.

faqs.question: How will new transport projects change commuting in Dubai?

data.answer: Upcoming transport-led Dubai projects are designed to significantly reduce travel times between emirates, improve last-mile connectivity within Dubai, and support long-term population growth by offering alternatives to commuting.

faqs.question: What role does sustainability play in new Dubai projects?

data.answer: Sustainability is a core focus across many Dubai projects, with developers integrating energy-efficient systems, water recycling, clean energy usage, and green mobility solutions into both infrastructure and mixed-use developments.

faqs.question: Which areas in Dubai are seeing the highest concentration of new mega projects?

data.answer: Dubai South, Dubai Creek Harbour, Zabeel Park, and key transport corridors are among the areas seeing a high concentration of large-scale Dubai projects, driven by long-term urban planning and infrastructure investment.
